tracks.narration: The tangent plane gets the slope right. To get the curvature right, add the Hessian.

Start in one variable. Pick a point. The constant approximation just holds f of a. The linear one adds the slope. The quadratic one adds one half f double prime, and the curve and the parabola lock together at the point.

In two variables, replace the slope with the gradient and replace the second derivative with the Hessian matrix. The quadratic term reads h transpose H h over two, where h is the displacement from the centre.

Pick a saddle-shaped surface and watch the approximation snap into focus. Order zero is flat. Order one tilts the plane to match the gradient — already much better. Order two adds the Hessian bowl, and the surface and the approximation hug the centre.
First order locks in slope. Second order locks in curvature. That is why the Hessian decides whether a critical point is a hill, a hollow, or a saddle.
